prediction.likelyOutcome: SPLC should prevail on the core unpaid-rent claim (already partially adjudicated) and on most, though probably not all, of the HTA double-rent claim for the holdover period; IPI's constructive eviction defense is factually weak given its retained keys, continued access, and eventual negotiated space reduction, but may shave some value off the double-rent component for the earlier padlocked months. Expect an award in the mid-to-high range of SPLC's own stated $787,436.01 trial request, plus a separately-litigated attorney's fee award under both the lease and the HTA.

outcome.description: On partial summary judgment the court awarded $243,600 rent for March 2020 to May 2021, $17,052 interest and $6,701 utilities ($267,353; the procedural history swaps the interest and utilities labels, the damages section and conclusion confirm them). After the January 11, 2023 bench trial the court rejected the constructive-eviction defense, held double rent accrued only from August 1, 2021 after the July 28, 2021 notice, and awarded a further $431,861 rent and double rent for June 1, 2021 to September 21, 2022 and $67,381.33 interest at 1% per month on the balance excluding double rent, entering judgment for $766,595.33 ($675,461 rent, $84,433.33 interest, $6,701 utilities) plus post-judgment interest and attorney's fees to be set on motion.
outcome.finalNote: No appeal reflected in the source. Amount verified against the conclusion. It includes the 1%-per-month interest ($84,433.33) because the court awarded it as part of the damages and the landlord's own demands ($787,436.01 at trial) include it, as the set does for other lease judgments with contract-rate interest (e.g. GSL Investments, Slyce); without interest the award is $682,162. Fees awarded, amount not stated.
